data.name: Makeen
data.gender_notes: Makeen is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'Makan', meaning 'place' or 'location', Makeen signifies a place of shelter, protection, and security. This name is mentioned in the Quran when Allah (swt) promises Prophet Ibrahim (as) that He will give him a place (makeen) and multiply his descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky. Makeen is an evocative name for a child, reminding parents of their role as protectors and providers, and Allah's promise of eternal security in the hereafter.
data.etymology: Makeen belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Shelter, Protection.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Makeen total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

The name Makeen is often associated with the qualities of piety, devotion, and spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Makeen was the name of a city in ancient Arabia that was an important early Islamic trade center. It was located near the present-day city of Al-Madinah Al-Munawwara in Saudi Arabia.
historical_references.context: Makeen was an important hub for commerce between Syria, Iraq, and Yemen. It was also the site of several significant battles during the Ridda Wars, a series of conflicts between the early Muslim community and the Arab tribes who had rejected Islam.

historical_references.reference: Makeen is also the name of a significant battle that took place in 624 CE during the early Islamic period. It is considered one of the first major military engagements of Muhammad and the early Muslims against their enemies in Mecca.
historical_references.context: The Battle of Makeen, also known as the Battle of the Trench, marked a turning point in the early Islamic history as the Muslims successfully defended themselves against a large Meccan army. The victory boosted the morale of the Muslim community and helped consolidate the early Islamic state.
